svg.title: Three security models: perimeter, session and transaction, zero trust
svg.desc: Perimeter security protects only the edge, leaving east-west traffic open. Session and transaction security pins users and devices and authorises every session. Zero trust adds real-time capture and analytics so each identity, device, application and the data itself carries a continuously updated trust score.
svg.text: Security moved from the edge of the network to every decision inside it
The three models are historical stages, not alternatives you may pick freely — each one answers a question the previous one could not
1 · PERIMETER "turtle shell"
· Firewalls at the perimeter only
· Inside is wide open, east-west traffic
is implicitly trusted
· Insider threats flourish
Protects: the entry points — nothing lateral
2 · SESSION & TRANSACTION
· Evolved from perimeter security
· Users and devices are pinned down
· Policy follows device, user, location
· 100% authentication + 100% authorisation
Protects: every session and transaction
3 · ZERO TRUST ARCHITECTURE
· Adds real-time capture and analytics
· AI/ML decisions made in real time
· Trust score per identity, device, app,
server, service and the data itself
Protects: the flows and the data, continuously
What gets inspected: the entry point → every session and transaction → every flow plus the data, all the time.
What trust means: binary, inside vs outside → authenticated identity → a number that rises and falls with observed behaviour.
The design consequence: security is not a box at the edge of the diagram. It is a decision made again at every later chapter — segmentation,
encryption, control-plane protection, management access — which is why the guide treats it as a design principle before it treats it as a technology.
